name: UCI-HAR leave-one-person-out benchmark
description: This letter addresses the problem of human activity recognition (HAR) of people wearing inertial sensors using data from the UCI-HAR dataset. We propose a light residual network, which obtains an F1-Score of 97.6% that outperforms previous works, while drastically reducing the number of parameters by a factor of 15, and thus the training complexity. In addition, we propose a new benchmark based on leave-one (person)-out cross-validation to standardize and unify future classifications on the same dataset, and to increase reliability and fairness in the comparisons.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark on a small public dataset; original UCI-HAR splits can leak subject information so the published leave-one-person-out (LOPO) split reduces contamination and increases fairness; susceptible to overfitting due to small sample of subjects.
